data.title: Unit 12: The solar system
The sun and the planets
data.text: The Sun is a star made up of burning gases.
About 70% of the Sun is hydrogen gas and most of the remaining part is helium.
It takes about 8 minutes for light from the Sun to reach Earth.
The Sun is about one million times bigger than the Earth.
The Sun is about five billion years old and has constantly been burning ever since.
On the surface of the Sun, huge explosions called solar flares occur from time to time.
There are also some dark spots on the Sun called sunspots.
Gas particles released from the Sun sometimes enter the Earth's atmosphere, causing solar winds.
In the northern polar regions they are called the Northern Lights.
In the south polar regions they are called Southern Lights.
